Dear Ms Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June for the flat I recently vacated.

As you know, I removed all of my belongings and moved out on 31 May, and I was not living at the property at any point in June. I was unable to get to your office to return the keys until 8 June, which I understand is why the rent for those eight days was charged.

If you are able to agree to this, I would be grateful if you could send the refund to my usual account, the details of which you already hold.

Thank you for your consideration, and for your help throughout my tenancy. I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your new address]
[Phone / email]

Dear Ms Norr,

I am writing regarding the rent charged for 1 to 8 June for the flat I rented from you.

I vacated the property and removed all of my belongings on 31 May, and the flat was empty from that date onward. As I was unable to reach your office until 8 June, I returned all keys on that day. I understand that under our signed agreement rent continues until the keys are handed back, and I appreciate that you have charged only for the period up to 8 June accordingly.

If you are able to do so, please send the refund to my usual bank account, the details of which you already hold.

Thank you for your consideration, and for your help throughout my tenancy.

Yours sincerely,
[Your name]
[Your new address]
[Phone / email]

Kind regards,
[Your name]

Answer:

Dear Orla,

I hope you're doing well. I wanted to ask about something before I move out on 30 June — I'd love your permission to repaint the living room myself on the weekend before I leave.

I'd be using the original pale grey colour, so it should look just as it did when I moved in. The flat has been a lovely home and I'd really like to hand it back looking cared for.

I know from your moving-out email that your decorator is coming on 2 July to repaint the living room anyway, so please don't feel this is necessary on my part — I'd simply like to do it as a gesture of goodwill. Of course, if you'd rather the decorator handle everything, I completely understand.

Just let me know what you think, and thanks so much for everything over the past while.

Warm regards,
[Your name]

Note: Since her decorator is already booked at her expense, she may decline — but that's fine, as the letter makes clear it's optional.

Answer: Dear Orla,

Of course, if you'd rather I leave the walls as they are since the decorator is coming so soon, that's completely fine — I just wanted to check with you first.

Thanks so much, and please let me know what you think.

Warm regards,
[Your name]
